title: Dan Moody and north-shore jobs
summary: Ernie describes Madisonville trombonist and bassist Dan Moody, a pickup-band leader who worked the Mandeville pavilion and fairs, and the jobs they played together later.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Did you ever know Dan Moody?

Oh yes, Dan Moody from Madisonville, he played trombone and bass. Matter of fact he just died about a year or two years ago. Can you tell us anything about him? Not in particular, I didn't play with Dan until 1952, let me see, it was the year that President Roosevelt died. I happened to be in the beauty spring, he'd come here to get me to play a job with him, and we played over there. You don't know what? And he had been playing with different fellas we'd make up groups from out of Punchitula and Covington, he had a piano player live in company, he'd go around and pick them up and they would play at this Duvors pavilion in Manderville. See, that's where this boat used to land from at the Millenbury, they'd catch these boats and they had that excursion every and Sunday with the Susquehanna. Little Susquehanna. And they would land at the Duvors place, well that place stood up till the last part of 1953 or something like that. Yeah. And he had a regular job there off and on and he would play in Buggaloosa, but he never kept in a regular group. He would go around and pick up different fellas.
He used to come here and get Sheep to go to the Covington Fair with him.
Yeah, Sheep used to play. You went over with Sheep and her body?
Yeah, out in Franklin. She used to go out there in Franklin and play with him on those fairs, Covington too. He played quite a few jobs there with him.
